chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: I may be in salat (prayer) and feel a cramp in my stomach, or discomfort, or throbbing. So he said: Turn away, then perform wudu (ablution), and build upon what has passed of your salat (prayer), so long as you have not invalidated the salat (prayer) by speaking deliberately. And if you spoke forgetfully, then there is no harm upon you; it is like one who speaks in salat (prayer) forgetfully. I said: What if he turns his face away from the qiblah? He said: Yes, even if he turns his face away from the qiblah.

So this report does not contradict what we have previously presented of the reports, because there is nothing in the report beyond that he found discomfort in his stomach, and not everyone who finds discomfort has entered a state of hadath. There is nothing in the report stating that he actually passed hadath. As for his statement, “so long as he has not invalidated the salat (prayer) deliberately,” it does not indicate that if he was forgetful then repetition is not required, except by way of an implication of wording; and such implication may be left aside, according to those who accept it, on account of other evidence. We have already shown that through the preceding reports. As for his ordering him to perform wudu (ablution), that may be understood as carrying a sense of recommendation. It is also possible that this was specific to speech, because one who speaks forgetfully is not required to repeat. For that reason he said immediately after this statement, “And if you spoke forgetfully, then there is no harm upon you,” which indicates that by his statement, “so long as he has not invalidated the salat (prayer) deliberately,” he intended deliberate invalidation by speech and not anything else.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act under discussion
key_terms.الْكَلَامِ: speech that may invalidate salat (prayer) if done deliberately
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), here discussed in relation to recommendation or ruling

ai.seo_question: If someone feels stomach discomfort during salat (prayer), can they leave and then continue the prayer?
ai.summary: This report discusses a person who feels abdominal discomfort during salat (prayer) and the ruling on leaving and resuming the prayer. The accompanying discussion clarifies that the narration does not prove actual hadath, and that its wording is interpreted in light of other reports concerning what invalidates salat (prayer), especially deliberate speech.
